key_insight: Boron redistributes toward defects in TiAl, pinning dislocations and suppressing deformation twinning to increase high-temperature strength.
engineering_relevance: Controlling boron content and defect populations could help engineers strengthen TiAl alloys while accounting for brittle boride phases and interface-dependent adhesion.
method: Developed a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential.
Combined grand-canonical Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations.
Analyzed boron segregation, defect interactions, and deformation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Polycrystalline TiAl simulations showed a 9.4% increase in average flow stress at 1 at.% boron and 900 K, accompanied by reduced shear strain accumulation.
watch_item: The reported strengthening is simulation-based; experimental validation is needed to establish performance under practical processing and loading conditions.
paper_title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
